sentences.text: As the instant matter is arising out of matrimonial dispute, a Coordinate Bench vide order dated 13.08.2024 referred the matter to the Mediation Centre of this Court.

For ready reference order dated 13.08.2024 is reproduced hereinbelow:-
"1. Heard Sri Pankaj Dwivedi along with Sri Yogesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Satya Prakash, learned counsel appearing for the informant and learned A.G.A. appearing for the State respondents.

2. The petitioners, by means of this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, has invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court with prayer to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 19.6.2024 registered as Case Crime No.
226 of 2024 under Sections 498A, 323, 354B, 504, 506, 307, 406 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Colonalganj, District Prayagraj.
3.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the present matter relates to matrimonial dispute, which may be amicably settled by way of mediation and conciliation.

Learned counsel for the petitioners states that there is every possibility of mediation in the present case, therefore, the matter may be referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court.

4. Since both the parties are represented, there is no need to issue notice to private contesting respondent no. 4.
5.

Learned counsel for the parties agreed that the parties shall remain present before the Mediation Centre of this Court on 24.8.2024.
6.

In view of the above, it is directed that petitioners shall deposit a sum of Rs.10,000/- by the next date fixed before the Mediation Centre of this Court, which shall be retained by the Mediation Centre as mediation fee.

7. The matter is remitted to the Mediation Centre with the direction that after deposit of such amount, by the petitioners, it shall fix 24.8.2024 for mediation and shall make all possible efforts to conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously.

8. Put up this case as fresh on 4.9.2024 along with the mediation centre report before the appropriate Bench.
9.
Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners in the above mentioned case.

10. It is made clear that in case there occurs default by the petitioners either in depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed,
the interim order shall cease to operate and the Mediation Centre shall immediately Bharat Tiwari And 5 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23942467/
2 communicate with the office which in turn shall list the case within a week before the appropriate Bench for passing orders in the matter."
4. Pursuant to the aforesaid order, both the parties appeared before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre and eventually, settled the dispute and a settlement agreement was prepared on 31.08.2024,
which is evident from report dated 01.09.2024 sent by Registrar, AHCMCC.

The terms of settlement agreement dated 31.08.2024 are being reproduced below for ready reference:-
"(a) That it is stated by the parties that real name of the Respondent no.4-Wife is Akansha Pandey instead of Akansha Panday as mentioned in the array of the parties of the present case.
(b) That the parties agreed to live separately and mutually settled to dissolve their marriage by filing a divorce petition u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court, Prayagraj within a week from today and they will produce certified copy of the aforesaid divorce petition before the Centre at the time of final settlement i.e. 21.09.2024.

(c) That it has been agreed between the parties that Bharat Tiwari (Petitioner No.1-Husband) shall pay an amount of Rs.36,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Six Lakh only)
to Akansha Panday (Respondent no.4-Wife) which includes permanent alimony,
Stridhan and maintenance of wife by way of demand drafts drawn in her favour.

(d) That it has been agreed between the parties that on the next date fixed i.e.
21.09.2024, the applicant no.1-husband shall bring a demand draft of Rs.18,00,000/-
(Rupees Eighteen Lakh only) in the name of Akansha Pandey (Respondent No.4-Wife) and the same shall be handed over to the Respondent No.4-Wife at the time of final settlement-agreement.

(e) That it has been agreed between the parties that the remaining amount i.e.
Rs.18,00,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakh only) will be paid by the husband to the wife by way of Demand Draft at the time of final judgment/second motion in the divorce petition before the Family Court, Prayagraj.
(f) That it has been agreed between the parties that the cases filed by them against each other will be kept in abeyance during this intervening period.
(g) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall appear again before the Centre on 21.09.2024."

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners states that in the light of settlement agreement dated 31.08.2024, the first petitioner (husband) has already deposited a demand draft bearing no.031635 of Rs.18 lakh drawn at UCO Bank in favour of his wife, Akansha Pandey (respondent no.4) and for the remaining amount, another demand draft of Rs.18 lakh had been submitted before the Bharat Tiwari And 5 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23942467/
3 competent court i.e. Court of Principal Judge, Family Court.

sentences.text: He further submits that once the parties have already settled the dispute amicably and in lieu of the settlement agreement, demand draft of Rs.36 lakh has already been deposited by the first petitioner in favour of his wife (respondent no.4), the impugned FIR is liable to be quashed.

He further states that in spite of deposit of demand draft of total Rs.36 lakh as per terms of the settlement agreement, till date informant/respondent no.4 had not turned up before the Principal Judge, Family Court for recording her statement in the on going proceedings under Section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (in short, Act, 1955') and due to her non-cooperation, further proceedings has been put to halt.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the informant/respondent no.4 fairly states that at present he has no information as to whether petitioner no.1 has deposited the subsequent demand draft of Rs.18 lakh to the court below or not.

He states that some time may be accorded to get appropriate instructions in this respect and also to apprise this Court about the present status of the on going proceedings under Section 13B of the Act, 1955.
7. Learned A.G.A. submits that once the parties have already amicably settled the dispute through mediation, he has no objection, in case the impugned FIR is quashed by this Court.

8. It is jointly submitted by learned counsel for both the sides that this being an offshoot of a matrimonial dispute, and when the same has come to an amicable settlement, the pending proceedings would serve no purpose and the same is liable to be quashed in the light of the judgements of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana and others,
2003(4) SCC 675, and Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, 2012(10) SCC 303.
9. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of B.S Joshi (supra) has held that in case the matrimonial dispute has come to an end, under a compromise/settlement, between the parties, then notwithstanding anything contained under Section 320 IPC, there is no legal impediment for this court to quash the proceedings of Section 498-A I.P.C etc, which has matrimonial flavour under its inherent powers in view of the recorded settlement between the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh (supra) has held in para-61 that;
"the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences Under Section 320 of the Code.

Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.

Such offences are not Bharat Tiwari And 5 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23942467/
4 private in nature and have serious impact on society.

sentences.text: Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil favour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile,
civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

10. Since the dispute between the parties have already been settled amicably vide settlement agreement dated 31.08.2024, the pending proceedings would serve no purpose and the same is liable to be quashed in the light of the aforesaid judgments.
11.

Consequently, the writ petition is allowed and the impugned First Information Report dated 19.06.2024 registered as Case Crime No.226 of 2024, under Section 498A, 323, 354B, 504, 506,
307, 406 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.Colnalganj, District-Allahabad as well as
all consequential proceedings are hereby quashed.

12. However, learned counsel for the respondent no.4/informant is given liberty to file an application for recall of this order, in case, it is found that the first petitioner has not deposited the entire amount in terms of settlement agreement dated 31.08.2024.
